title: The Classic of Purity
altTitles: The Classic of Purity and Rest
Taishang Laojun shuo chang qingjing jing
dateDisplay: Tang dynasty recension of earlier material
attributionNote: The scripture is presented as the teaching of the Most High Lord Lao to the Perfected One of the Eastern Florescence. Its date is uncertain; the received text is usually placed in the Tang and was transmitted with a commentary attributed to Ge Xuan.
description: The Classic of Purity is one of the most widely recited short scriptures of Daoism: a compact teaching on the pure and still heart as the root of the Dao, on the desires and disturbances that obscure it, and on the return to stillness in which the true Dao is known. It is chanted in temples and used as a primer of Daoist contemplation, and its phrases circulate far beyond monastic settings.
historicalContext: The Qingjing jing was transmitted with a commentary ascribed to Ge Xuan and became a standard liturgical and devotional text in the Tang and Song. Legge printed a translation among the appendixes to his second volume of Texts of Taoism (1891), where it illustrates the devotional literature that grew around the philosophical classics.
availabilityNote: Complete. Legge's translation of the classic is streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time; it is a single short page, presented here as one chapter. The appendixes and notes of the volume are not part of the work.
